categories.main_business_segments: Consolidated Edison, Inc. (Con Edison) operates through four main business segments: (1) Consolidated Edison Company of New York, Inc. (CECONY), which provides regulated electric, gas, and steam delivery services in New York City and Westchester County; (2) Orange & Rockland Utilities, Inc. (O&R), which provides regulated electric and gas delivery services in southeastern New York and northern New Jersey; (3) Con Edison Clean Energy Businesses, Inc., which develops, owns, and operates renewable energy infrastructure projects and provides energy-related products and services (held for sale as of December 31, 2022); and (4) Con Edison Transmission, Inc., which invests in electric transmission projects and manages both electric and gas assets.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The core operations rely on extensive electric, gas, and steam distribution infrastructure, including the largest underground electric delivery system in the U.S. for CECONY. The company utilizes advanced metering infrastructure (AMI), distributed energy resources (DER), and energy storage technologies. Clean Energy Businesses focus on utility-scale solar and wind generation, often underpinned by long-term power purchase agreements, and employ tax equity financing structures. Transmission investments are made in partnership with other utilities and through joint ventures.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Primary customers are residential, commercial, and industrial users in New York City, Westchester County, southeastern New York, and northern New Jersey. The company also serves government and municipal entities, including the New York Power Authority (NYPA). Clean Energy Businesses serve wholesale and retail customers, including utilities and municipalities, across the U.S. through renewable energy projects.
categories.geographic_coverage: Con Edison’s regulated utility operations are concentrated in New York City, Westchester County, southeastern New York, and northern New Jersey. Clean Energy Businesses have renewable energy projects across the United States. Transmission investments are focused in New York State, with some interests in projects in the Mid-Atlantic and Midwest regions.
categories.supply_chain_position: The company operates primarily as a downstream utility, delivering electricity, gas, and steam to end users. It does not own significant generation assets (except for steam-related cogeneration and some renewable assets through Clean Energy Businesses, which are being divested). In transmission, it participates as a midstream investor and operator through joint ventures.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Con Edison’s strategic focus is on supporting the clean energy transition, grid modernization, and resilience against climate change. The company invests heavily in infrastructure upgrades, energy efficiency, electrification (including electric vehicles), distributed energy resources, and advanced metering. R&D initiatives include demonstration projects for distributed system platforms, energy storage, and integration of renewables, as well as climate adaptation planning.
categories.revenue_model: The primary revenue model is regulated cost-of-service utility delivery, where rates are set by state regulators to recover costs and provide a return on capital. Utilities recover energy supply costs from customers with no markup. Clean Energy Businesses generate revenue from long-term power purchase agreements, energy-related services, and wholesale market sales. Transmission revenues are earned through regulated returns on invested capital.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Con Edison is one of five major investor-owned utilities in New York State, alongside National Grid, Avangrid, National Fuel Gas Company, and CH Energy Group. It is the dominant utility in New York City and Westchester. In renewables, Clean Energy Businesses compete with other independent power producers and utilities. The company faces increasing competition from distributed generation, energy efficiency, and electrification alternatives, but enjoys strong regulatory protection in its core utility territories.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For 2022, Con Edison reported $15.7 billion in operating revenues and $1.66 billion in net income. The company’s assets totaled $69.1 billion at year-end. The utility segments provide the vast majority of earnings and are expected to drive future growth, especially as the Clean Energy Businesses are divested. Capital investments are projected at $4.8–$5.0 billion annually through 2025, with a stable, regulated growth profile and a focus on infrastructure modernization.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Con Edison emphasizes safe, reliable, and resilient energy delivery, with a strong commitment to supporting New York’s clean energy and climate goals. Its value proposition includes best-in-class reliability, extensive underground infrastructure, and leadership in grid modernization and clean energy integration. The company differentiates itself through its scale, regulatory stability, and proactive investments in sustainability, customer experience, and climate adaptation.
